J-1.title: From an empty series to a scored matchday

J-1.1.what: 12 clubs exist; none is public yet

J-1.10.what: 16 races entered; the points add up to what 16 races hand out

J-1.11.what: the series table has the act in it, every club with its placement

J-1.12.what: the configuration is frozen; a typo in the title is still fixable

J-1.13.what: a winner disqualified; the points follow on write

J-1.15.what: the draw is refused with `event-not-ready`, carrying the same codes

J-1.16.what: team count and date fixed; the event is ready

J-1.2.what: "Lifecycle Trophy 2026" with the 12 clubs, as a draft — 404 publicly

J-1.3.what: the series is published and listed

J-1.4.what: the event exists with a title and boats; the series' registrations are its entries

J-1.5.what: the readiness lists what is missing: team count, date

J-1.6.what: a pairing list from the catalog; a second draw replaces it

J-1.7.what: the event is in the public calendar

J-1.8.what: the pairing list prints — or the server says it cannot, never silently

J-2.title: A new club gets going and runs itself

J-2.1.what: the club exists, its address made from the abbreviation

J-2.10.what: the club is in the public list, and its page shows the series

J-2.2.what: the club is not in the public club list — it competes nowhere yet

J-2.3.what: the account exists (verified by administration) and holds `admin` on the club

J-2.4.what: my space lists the club, with the relation `admin`

J-2.5.what: the crest is stored; the club's `logo_url` points at it

J-2.6.what: refused with `last-organizer` (409); the club keeps its admin

J-2.7.what: the person holds `manager` on the club — no acceptance step

J-2.8.what: an application for the series, status `requested`; still not public

J-2.9.what: accepted: the club is a participant of the series

J-3.1.what: refused with 404 — nobody is on record under the address; nobody is added

J-3.10.what: the membership is gone; the club is no longer in my space; the person record stays

J-3.11.what: a person of the club with an address and no account — an active member at once (a new person is in no club)

J-3.12.what: an invitation mailed from the person's row — a one-use link for 14 days

J-3.13.what: an account with the address verified by the link, linked to the club's person record; the membership `active` — account first, then the club; signed in

J-3.14.what: after confirming what follows: a mail with a one-use link for 14 days; the person is on record, *pending* (`invited`) — in no squad, not a member

J-3.15.what: another club's invitation to that address is refused (`invitation-pending`, 409), naming no club

J-3.16.what: the inviting club's admin resends: a new link for 14 days, the earlier one dead

J-3.2.what: an account exists, its address only claimed; a code is mailed — the same answer for a known address

J-3.3.what: the address is verified; the account has its own person record (#40), no role and no club

J-3.4.what: a password is set; signing in with it gives a token

J-3.5.what: an active membership of the person — at once, no acceptance step while they are in no other club

J-3.6.what: my space lists the club with the chip *member*; the person record has no date of birth yet

J-3.7.what: the roster shows the club's people by display name, no email

J-3.8.what: the member's person record carries a date of birth — the club's to change, being its member

J-3.9.what: their own record (`Person.user_id`) carries the corrected name and date

J-4.title: An organizer sets up a series

J-4.1.what: the series exists with its year and squad limits, no clubs, as a draft — 404 publicly

J-4.2.what: the person holds `manager` on the series; their admin list shows this series and no other

J-4.3.what: the series has its dates and its clubs; creating another series is refused (403)

J-4.4.what: an application, `requested` — not among the series' clubs

J-4.6.what: act 1 exists with its host club; the series' clubs, the accepted one included, are its entries

J-4.8.what: the series is listed for its year and its table opens

J-5.title: A club's crew is cleared for a matchday

J-5.1.what: the squad is saved on the club's series registration, within the series' maximum

J-5.12.what: a `guardian` confirmation with the scan; the sailor is cleared

J-5.13.what: the same, recorded by the team manager for a form the club collected

J-5.14.what: the check-in list shows every squad member `cleared`, nothing outstanding, the minors' scans on file

J-5.15.what: the parent holds `guardian` on the sailor — only the child's club may link

J-5.16.what: a `guardian_online` confirmation from the parent's own account; the minor is cleared, nothing on paper

J-5.17.what: the club's card in the manager's my space shows `crew_waiver_missing` — the crew stays named, nothing is locked

J-5.2.what: below the series' minimum: the squad says `squad_min`, my space shows `squad_below_min` — and it is saved

J-5.3.what: the squad reaches the minimum; the need is gone

J-5.4.what: the squad is saved on the event entry, within the event's own limits

J-5.5.what: the crew is named for the matchday — only from the squad

J-5.6.what: each sailor's my space shows `waiver` on the series (or the stand-alone event)

J-5.7.what: the age can be judged; until then the page says "add your date of birth first" and confirming is refused (`waiver-birth-date-required`)

J-5.8.what: an `online` confirmation of the version in force; the sailor is cleared for every event of the series

J-5.9.what: the form PDF with the wording, name, date of birth and competition; an online click is refused (`guardian-confirmation-needed`)

J-6.title: From a sailed race to the report and the press release

J-6.1.what: the race is scored: the act's public page counts one more race (`races_scored`)

J-6.10.what: the league's media page shows the act's photos with their credit

J-6.11.what: the pictures are in the library, the act's, under editorial's credit

J-6.2.what: an upload link for the act exists; the key is shown once and says what its pictures are for

J-6.3.what: the pictures are in the library, the act's, under the link's credit

J-6.4.what: the report is a draft about the act, its picture from the library — 404 publicly

J-6.5.what: the preview shows the report with the act's photos at its end; nothing is stored

J-6.7.what: the press release is published for the league

J-6.8.what: the league's news lists the report; its page ends with the act's photos

J-6.9.what: the league's press centre lists the release, and its text opens

J-7.title: From a claim to the bank

J-7.1.what: the person holds `treasurer` on the club — and so on every event the club hosts

J-7.10.what: the changed item makes the claim a draft; submitted again, it waits on the treasurer again

J-7.11.what: the organizer may decide the helper's claim, but their own is refused (`claim-own-decision`) and not on their list

J-7.12.what: `approved` at the claimed amount; the claim is frozen and on the list to pay

J-7.13.what: the code carries the claim's copied account, the open amount and the line `C-<id> …`; never for the claimant

J-7.14.what: one settled payment: the claim is `paid`, off the list, and has no code any more (`claim-not-payable`)

J-7.15.what: one `issued` payment per payee; the claim reads `in_payment` and leaves the list to pay

J-7.16.what: a pain.001.001.09 file: the club's IBAN as debtor, the helper's as creditor, the claim in the remittance line

J-7.17.what: the bank has the file and the treasurer's TAN

J-7.18.what: the run is settled; the claim reads `paid`

J-7.19.what: the payment is `failed` with its reason; the claim is approved and `unpaid`, back on the list to pay

J-7.2.what: the club's account (holder, IBAN, BIC from the IBAN) is saved; only the treasurer and the club's admin read it

J-7.20.what: the next run pays the claim again

J-7.3.what: the person holds `helper` on the event — the host club's admin is the event's admin; no power on the event, but a claim on it

J-7.4.what: the helper's account is saved, checked by `schwifty`; only they read it

J-7.5.what: the event is among the helper's claim targets; a draft claim with a hotel item over a range of dates — submitting it now is refused, the invoice is missing (`expense-document-missing`)

J-7.6.what: the invoice is on the item, checked by content, under a random name

J-7.7.what: `submitted`; the payer is the host club, holder and IBAN copied onto the claim

J-7.8.what: the claim is on the treasurer's list, to decide, and its receipt opens for them

J-7.9.what: `rejected` with the message; the helper's my space shows `claim_rejected` on the event

J-8.title: A club hosts its own event

J-8.1.what: refused with `series-not-mine` (403): a club adds no act to a series it does not organize

J-8.10.what: the date is set; the readiness says `ready`

J-8.11.what: a pairing list from the catalog with both host teams and the accepted club, not the rejected one

J-8.13.what: 16 races entered; the host's manager may not enter a result (403) — organizing is not racing

J-8.15.what: the event's public page has the 12 teams' results, both host teams among them, its host club, and no series

J-8.2.what: the event exists with its host club, no series, no matchday, `teams_per_club` 2, as a draft; no club entered; every club is a candidate; its creator organizes it through `manager from host_club`

J-8.3.what: the person holds `race_officer` on the event — written by the host club's admin (`admin from host_club`); the host's manager may not write it (403)

J-8.4.what: the event is published and in the public calendar, `series` empty — the field is not complete, and need not be

J-8.5.what: nine invited clubs and the host club twice (`<short name>` and `<short name> 2`) are entered; a third host team is refused (`too-many-teams-per-club`)

J-8.6.what: an application to the event, `requested` — not an entry: the readiness still says `pairing-team-count-mismatch`

J-8.7.what: the host's manager sees the event's applications and accepts: the club is entered

J-8.9.what: `rejected`, and the applying club reads the reason in its own list

J-9.1.what: the league's current year is open; while an act is live its *Results* chapter opens the page and names the act

J-9.2.what: the act's page is open on *Results* — racing has begun — and every tab has its own address

J-9.3.what: the interim standing of the act: every entered team ranked, its points per flight sailed

J-9.4.what: the draw: every race with its boats by colour, each team once per flight; a club not entered has no seat

J-9.5.what: one card per entered team with its crew, helm first; a crew not named yet says so; names only

J-9.6.what: the sailor's page: the series registration and this act's lineup, no contact details

J-9.7.what: the name stays in the crew as plain text; the page answers 404 like nobody at all

J-9.8.what: the year's table: a column per act, the running act counted, each heading leading to its act

J-9.9.what: the club that sat act 2 out carries its field size + 1 there, and the cell says so
